thesis: Microsoft's 29 Jul 2026 quarter settled the question the stock had been losing on all year - whether AI capex converts to revenue. Azure accelerated to +43% constant currency and crossed $100B for the fiscal year, and management guided +45% for the September quarter. Price structure still confirms, but the re-rating already happened in one 15% day, so this is a hold-and-let-it-work, not a fresh entry with an edge.
bull_case: FY26 Q4 (29 Jul 2026): revenue $90.01B, +18% y/y; EPS $4.74 vs $4.24 expected; Azure +43% cc, accelerating from +40%; Azure revenue disclosed above $100B for FY26, +41%. Guidance of +45% cc Azure for FY27 Q1 means acceleration is guided, not hoped for. Shares rose 15.5% on the print, the largest single-day market-value gain on record, off a base where the stock had been down ~19% year to date - so positioning was washed out, not crowded. Packet: close 499.7 above SMA50 above SMA200, 3m momentum +20.2%, score +0.55.
bear_case: The catalyst has already fired. There is no scheduled company event until FY27 Q1 results in late October, which is beyond the near end of this horizon, and the stock is holding a vertical gap that gap-fills badly if the market de-rates. RSI 63 is extended without being extreme. Azure growth is capex-funded and the same concentration and rate arguments that hit Nvidia hit here: AI-linked names are roughly 40-45% of index cap into a 16 Sep FOMC where a hike is more likely than not. I looked for company-specific red flags - dilution, insider selling, regulatory action - and found none material in the current period.
catalysts: FY27 Q1 results late Oct 2026: the +45% cc Azure guide is the test
16 Sep 2026 FOMC outcome and the path of the 10-year yield
Azure capacity and capex commentary at autumn investor events
risks: Gap-fill risk back toward the pre-print level if AI sentiment turns
Azure decelerating below 40% cc would break the whole thesis
Capex intensity compressing free cash flow
Rate shock on a high-multiple megacap
invalidation: A daily close below 470 (gives back the post-earnings gap and the SMA50 zone), or FY27 Q1 Azure growth guided or reported below 40% constant currency.
